recipes.name: Cream Puffs
ingredients_raw: 2 (3.5 ounce) packages instant vanilla pudding mix

steps.text: Combine cream, milk, and pudding mix in a bowl; cover the bowl with plastic wrap and refrigerate to set.
Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
Bring water and butter to a rolling boil in a large pot.
Stir in flour and salt until the mixture forms a ball.
Transfer dough to a large bowl; beat in eggs, one at a time, beating well after each using a wooden spoon or stand mixer.
Drop batter by tablespoonfuls onto an ungreased baking sheet, spaced about 2 inches apart.
Bake in the preheated oven until puffs are golden brown and centers are dry, 20 to 25 minutes. Let puffs cool.
When puffs are cool, split and fill with pudding mixture, or pipe pudding into shells use a pastry bag.

raw_recipe.headline: Cream Puffs
raw_recipe.description: Cream puffs made with choux pastry that puffs up when baked; fill with vanilla cream and drizzle melted chocolate on top for a crowd-pleasing dessert.

review.reviewBody: Wonderful recipe! Very light and delicious. A tip, though, for this and all cream puff recipes: After baking is finished, turn off the oven, crack the door open with a towel or potholder, and let stand in the oven for about an hour. This prevents them from sagging!

Simply delicious. Very easy to prepare. To cut down on clean up and to make filling the cream puffs a snap, put the pudding mix, milk and cream in a zip top bag. Shake and massage the mixture until uniform, then place in the refrigerator to set (this takes about 15 minutes or so). Once set, cut about 1/8 of an inch off the tip of the bag. This way, instead of trying to spoon the mixture into the cream puffs by hand, or transfering the mixture to a pastery bag, you can directly pipe the mixture into the puff. Be sure to cut only an 1/8 of an inch or so off the bag to ensure maximum control of the amount of filling you're putting into the puffs. Fill the mixture from the bottom of the puff by making a tiny incision (I used the tip of a steak knife), that way the puff will remain whole and look more appetizing when served (as opposed to slicing it in half and filling it like a sandwich).

This was so simple I have to say! And the cream filling is to die for, I added a little almond extract to mine. I brought this to work, and boy do they just think I'm the next best thing! If you've never made these before, a trick I used was to pipe the dough with a star tip into mini muffin tin. It helped control size and made it so easy to remove them. Plus the star tip gave them a pretty look! Great recipe! Thanks for sharing!

Simple and spectacular! I've made this recipe more than a half-dozen times so far, and it never fails to garner raves. A few notes from my kitchen: Letting the pastries cool slowly in the oven after baking -- I turn the oven off and prop the door ajar by a couple of inches -- keeps them from collapsing before I have a chance to fill them. A half-teaspoon of vanilla, almond, or orange extract added to the filling erases any processed taste that might linger from the pudding mix. Also, a drizzle of melted dark chocolate on top adds a scrumptious accent.

This recipe is perfect, but leaves out an important step: let the dough ball cool for 10-15 minutes before adding the eggs. Dough should get get down to 150-160 degrees F with an insta-read thermometer. I also let mine cool to room temp before adding the pastry cream. They were a huge hit!

The shells came out perfect but for the filling, I whipped the heavy cream to soft peaks, added the milk and pudding mix, an extra teaspoon of vanilla bean paste and 1/2 cup powdered sugar and continued to beat til it was a little more light and fluffy. Then used a pastry bag and tip to fill from the bottom. Dusted with powdered sugar to finish.

I think one of the most important tips that no one is mentioning, is ONCE YOU HAVE MADE YOUR SPOONFUL OF DOUGH, DON'T ADD TO IT. DON'T EVEN OUT THE BATTER. JUST LEAVE IT. WHATEVER YOU DO, DO NOT ADD THAT EXTRA LITTLE BIT OF BATTER ON TOP! And seriously, only add one egg at a time until it isn't shiny any more with each one.

I took the smart advise of another reviewer and when the timer went off I turned off the oven and cracked the door for an hour. With the filling, I added an equal part “sturdy” whipped cream (cream cheese and sugar added) for extra fluff. I made three flavors, mango, match, and cookies and cream!

This recipe was great. Easy to make and after reading some comments easy to cool without deflation. I made these a day ahead of needing them and put them in a covered container overnight. Big mistake! Huge! They got soggy and deflated. I simply made another batch and they were perfect. I used an idea from Chef John’s puff pastry swans and coated the bottoms of the puffs with chocolate ganache and then filled with Godiva white chocolate instant pudding for half and Godiva chocolate pudding for the other half. Fabulous.
 My missing star is due to the deflation after storing.

I made one batch and they were gone in under an hour! I have a lot of people in my family and they all loved it! I did mix the dough ball with an electric mixer to cool it before adding the eggs. I made it once without cooling the dough and the eggs cooked :( I also added vanilla and 1tsp sugar to the dough as suggested by others. I've made it in the past with chocolate pudding and people preferred the vanilla. SO GOOD.

This recipe was awesome! I cooled the dough before beating in the eggs as suggested in the reviews and another recipe I found, and baked them for about 35 mins as the insides were questionably done. I found that just after the flour was added and the dough formed, it was limp and sticky, like a thick paste instead of dough, but as it cooled , I thought to stir it to release the steam instead of let it lay there like a collapsed ball. After some time, it no longer seemed to emit steam, and I left it to cool. After baking, I filled them with whipped cream and dusted them with powdered sugar, giving them a decadent tase and an appearance suitable for a bakery showcase. My family was very impressed.
I have been making these several times in the last month and following the directions….come out …perfect!! I also made them with gluten free flour and could not tell the difference.
It has been a while since I made pate a cheux. I'd LOVE to say that these cream puffs were great. But all but FOUR stuck to the baking sheet! Parchment paper first! Ugh! It should have said that!
I followed Carolines advice and they came out perfect
absolutely yummy!
Really good. Loved it. Will definitely make again!!
Didn't puff. Burnt on bottom. Swimming in water.
The filling is amazing and would make a great custard for other uses!
Love love love these!!!! I tweaked the recipe a little by adding chocolate icing and strawberries!! YUUUMMMMM!!
Delicious! I made homemade Vanilla Cream from my mother's cookbook dated 1932. It takes time, but it was absolutely wonderful.
